title: Transparent kernel probing quarantine workflow and circuit-breaker for capacity surges
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Summary: During the 2026-02-27 capacity surge on eu-west-1 we observed sustained p95/p99 latency inflation caused by aggressive deterministic kernel probing executed by the scheduler. Probes intended to validate kernel compatibility started cascading: probes consumed batch slots and KV cache priming windows, interleaving with production requests and increasing tail latency. This ticket implements a quarantine and circuit-breaker workflow for kernel probes that (1) isolates probes from production execution pools, (2) enforces per-cluster probe budgets and adaptive backoff, and (3) makes probing behavior observable and configurable via the Console and runtime flags.
root_cause: Scheduler introduced deterministic probing that runs synchronously on every new model-path activation without backoff or collective rate limiting. Under load, probes contend for GPU queues and favor small probes that prevent larger production batches from coalescing, increasing serialization and p99 latency.

Run a staged rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automatic rollback on latency regressions: owner=Ravi Kapoor, ETA=2026-03-22, status=Planned
rollforward_plan: Merge probe-quarantine branch to canary runtime pool and monitor p95/p99 for 24h. If stable, proceed with staged rollout increments and continuously validate probe_quarantined_count metric. Coordinate with capacity team to keep burst buffer available during rollout.
rollback_plan: Feature flag the quarantine system. On regressions revert flag to 'off' and roll back changes via the control plane. If control-plane rollback is blocked, scale up Dedicated pool capacity as emergency mitigation while engineers revert changes in runtime.
